name: Server Calculation Round-Trip (send row → merge back → recalc)
description: The three-step shape used whenever a field edit requires server-side business logic (pricing, tax, unit conversion): send the current row/header to a stored proc, merge the returned row back into the same index, then splice in the shared recalculation fragment. Used by every editable non-derived field in the line-items grid.

proc.description: e.g. "FAMST.FAPO_Onchange". Module logic goes under FAMST.*, generic platform services under PWA.*.

argumentConventions.strXmlDetails: The row payload. "[this]" inside a row control serialises the whole current row. "[DsFrmDetails1.[this.propkey]]" is the equivalent explicit form (used inside fragments and deferred actions, where `this` may not bind as expected).
argumentConventions.strXmlHeader: The header payload. Either a purpose-built dataset ("[dsVATHeaderDetails]") or the whole header ("[DsFrmHeaderEntry]"). Purpose-built is preferable — it makes the proc's contract explicit.
argumentConventions.dsets: Always [{name, row:0, table:"Table"}]. row:0 takes the first row; "Table" is the default result-table name.
argumentConventions.mode: Single proc serving several call sites, discriminated by mode — FAPO_Onchange takes "details"; GetAccountDetails takes "GL" or "SL".

rules: The merge target index must match the row that was sent. Inside a row control use [this.propkey]; inside deferred/customevents actions use [dslist.rowindex].

Merging the WHOLE return dataset ("data": "[dsFAPOOnchange]") rather than naming fields is the convention — the proc decides which fields it owns. This means a proc can add an output field without any layout change.
Use onFocusOut, never whenchange, for anything that reaches the server.
